Evidence before equations

Data with a clear provenance.

Measured numbers anchor the questions. Simple models make the calculus visible.

Published values

Historical observations, long-term tidal datums, equipment dimensions, and operating capacities are identified individually.

Teaching assumptions

Density fields, shapes, pipe profiles, and force fields are invented unless explicitly identified otherwise. They are not field observations or engineering recommendations.

Exact mathematics

A symbolic answer can be exact for a model while the model remains an approximation. Report units and explain its limits.

Source pages were consulted November 17, 2026. Tide datums use the 1983–2001 epoch; river data are a historical March 2000 snapshot. No live ocean-current data are claimed.

Shared conversions

1 ft = 0.3048 m · 1 US gal = 0.003785411784 m³ · 1 acre = 4046.8564224 m² · 1 day = 86,400 s

Use Cartesian coordinates in the stated local units. Invented polygons are not actual reserve boundaries. All checker feedback concerns the stated model, not a real-world forecast.

How the practice tools work

Answers, completed checks, hints, and discussion notes are stored only in this browser’s local storage. Math is rendered by a bundled local copy of MathJax. The site has no accounts, analytics, external math-rendering requests, or AI API. Solutions and expected answers are intentionally included in the site files; this is a learning aid rather than a secure assessment.

If browser storage is unavailable, all questions, hints, solutions, and answer checks still work for the current visit. Use “Reset this week” to clear one week’s saved work.

The checker supports elementary expressions and samples equivalent formula inputs at several test points; it does not constitute a proof of symbolic equivalence or evaluate written reasoning. The vector-potential construction is checked by numerically differentiating its components at several points and comparing the curl; it also checks the requested zero first component. Written reasoning and theorem hypotheses still need your own justification.
